topic.title: How Do Bacteria Communicate?
topic.learning_objective: Understand how bacteria use chemical signals to communicate and coordinate behavior.

sections.narration: They use chemical signals called quorum sensing to determine their population density. These messages help them act together as a group.
Bacteria release molecules into their environment. Other bacteria pick up these signals and respond accordingly.

Scientists study this communication to fight infections and develop new treatments. Understanding it changes how we see microbial life.

closing.narration: Bacteria use chemical signals to work together, shaping their survival and influencing medical science in powerful ways.

full_narration:
Bacteria don’t just live—they talk.

They use chemical signals called quorum sensing to determine their population density. These messages help them act together as a group.

Bacteria release molecules into their environment. Other bacteria pick up these signals and respond accordingly.

They form protective biofilms or switch from harmless to harmful states. This coordination helps them survive in tough conditions.

Scientists study this communication to fight infections and develop new treatments. Understanding it changes how we see microbial life.

Bacteria use chemical signals to work together, shaping their survival and influencing medical science in powerful ways.
